newsitem.title: FRANCE: France condemns Mostar ethnic violence.
newsitem.headline: France condemns Mostar ethnic violence.

text.p: France on Tuesday condemned an outbreak of violence in the divided city of Mostar in which Bosnian Croats fired at a crowd of Moslems, and urged the two parties not to let the city's fragile peace be shattered.

"We strongly condemn the incidents in Mostar yesterday which involved hundreds of Moslems and Bosnian Croats. These incidents work against the efforts of the international community, and particularly the European Union, in this city," the Foreign Ministry said in a statement.

Monday's bloodshed, the worst in Mostar since NATO troops deployed in late 1995, occurred after 500 Moslem pilgrims heading to Liska cemetery on the Croat side of Mostar were blocked by 700 Croats who were taking part in a Roman Catholic carnival parade. At least one person died and 22 were wounded.
The ministry said French soldiers were involved with Spanish units sent in to separate the two sides. A dusk-to-dawn curfew was imposed on both sides of the town.

"The (ethnic groups) are responsible for keeping the peace in Bosnia-Herzegovina. It is therefore essential for them to see to it that reconciliation between the various communities is not called into question by the actions of isolated elements hostile to this peace process," the ministry said.
The United States, whose diplomacy ended a Moslem-Croat war in 1994 and set up a shaky bi-national federation, has also condemned the violence and implicitly blamed the Croats.
